quotes.text: Signature-based detection only catches what's already been seen. Modern attacks are adaptive, targeted, and often use brand new or custom malware.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up why traditional antivirus falls short against modern threats.

quotes.text: Prevention is the lock on your front door. And EDR is the motion sensor in your hallway that alerts you when someone's already inside.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear analogy for the difference between prevention and EDR.

quotes.text: It doesn't shut down the domain controller. Legitimate users keep authenticating normally. The attacker is blocked, but your business keeps running.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows how attack disruption contains threats without stopping critical infrastructure.

quotes.text: If you have E5, this is already paid for, you're leaving protection on the table if you don't turn it on.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: If you're a small team without dedicated security staff, the technology alone isn't enough. The system generates alerts. Someone needs to watch them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: An honest caveat that tooling needs people or an MDR service behind it.

chapters.title: Why antivirus is no longer enough
Defender for Endpoint: prevention, detection, response
How it fits into Microsoft Defender XDR

takeaways: Signature-based antivirus only catches known threats, so modern endpoint security has to watch behavior across every device, not just scan files.
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint combines next-generation protection, EDR, vulnerability management and automated investigation, and Plan 2 is already included in Microsoft 365 E5.
Integrated with Defender XDR, Intune and Sentinel, it correlates alerts into single incidents, but small teams still need people or an MDR service to watch and respond.
hook: Traditional antivirus can no longer keep up with ransomware, phishing and attackers who move quietly between devices. This plain-English episode is for IT admins and business owners who want to understand Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, from EDR and attack disruption to licensing and the first steps to turn it on.
